question: Regular-vs-Extended classification, and the Pre-Open treatment, for every BTIC, TAS, TAM, TACO and TMAC shape proposed in docs/plans/2026-09-05-cme-trade-type-handoff.md; and whether the globex_spot_quoted sourced-absence precedent can be applied per shape.
answer_short: No BTIC, TAS, TAM, TACO or TMAC shape has a regular (pit/RTH) session in any era the crate models. Every one ships regular: &[], its whole published executable window in extended, and its own group Pre-Open in order_entry. The globex_spot_quoted precedent is not merely met but superseded: CME's own structured product data states the negative affirmatively per root (all 234 trade-type product records carry floor "-", floorVol "0" and a venues string with no Floor component), and the ContractSpecs API demonstrably has an "Open Outcry:" venue label - it prints one for SOFR options - and never attaches it to a trade-type hours line. One correction to the previous pass: NYMEX & COMEX Rule 524.A.1 DID carry a pit route for TAS from 2009-09-14 until a 2015-03-06..2016-08-09 bracket, but CME lists that route under the UNDERLYING's product code while the Globex TAS root has its own commodity-code table, so it is a pricing convention in the underlying's pit and not a session of the instrument this crate keys.

states.artifact: CME Group Market Regulation Advisory Notice RA2302-5, "TAS, TAM, BTIC, TACO, and TMAC Transactions" (Rule References: Rule 524) - Section 3, "Entry of TAS, TAM, BTIC, TACO, and TMAC Orders on CME Globex"
states.artifact_date: Advisory Date July 13, 2023; Effective Date July 31, 2023 (both stated in the notice's own header block)
states.capture_ts: 2026-09-06T05:15:01Z (Pass 1 capture; bytes re-verified against the recorded sha256 and re-read in full this pass, 2026-09-06T06:16Z)
states.verbatim: "Rule 524 permits the initiation of TAS, TAM, BTIC, TACO, and TMAC orders into CME Globex only subsequent to the beginning of each group's pre-open state and during the time period the applicable contracts are available for TAS, TAM, BTIC, TACO, or TMAC trading on CME Globex, as applicable. The initiation of any TAS, TAM, BTIC, TACO or TMAC order on CME Globex outside of these time periods is strictly prohibited." Immediately following: "Market participants are reminded that the timing of each groups' pre-open state may be randomized, as described in the Client Systems Wiki, available here." And, further down the same section: "Any market participant who initiates the entry of a TAS, TAM, BTIC, TACO or TMAC order prior to receipt of the security status message indicating that the market has transitioned to the pre-open will be subject to disciplinary action ... notwithstanding that the order may have been rejected by the CME Globex system."
states.bears_on: Splits each shape's day into exactly the crate's two executable-adjacent phases: order INITIATION is permitted from the beginning of that group's own pre-open state, and EXECUTION is confined to the period the contracts are 'available for ... trading'. That is `order_entry` then `extended`. The words 'each group's pre-open state' also establish that a TAS/TAM/BTIC/TACO/TMAC group has its OWN pre-open, separate from the underlying's.

states.artifact: RA2302-5 Section 6, "Text of CME, CBOT, and NYMEX/COMEX Rule 524" - the rule that creates all five shapes
states.artifact_date: Advisory Date July 13, 2023; Effective Date July 31, 2023
states.verbatim: CME/CBOT 524.A.1 (TAS): "A TAS order may be entered on Globex at any time the applicable contract is available for TAS trading on Globex and during such TAS-eligible contract's prescribed pre-open time period. The initiation of any TAS order on Globex outside these time periods is prohibited." 524.A.2: "...may be executed as a block trade pursuant to the requirements of Rule 526 or as an Exchange of Futures for Physical (“EFP”) or Exchange of Futures for Risk (“EFR”) transaction pursuant to the requirements of Rule 538." The identical two-clause structure is repeated verbatim for 524.B.1 (BTIC), 524.C.1 (TACO), 524.D.1 (TMAC) and, under NYMEX/COMEX, 524.A.1 (TAS) and 524.B.1 (TAM) - each naming Globex plus the block/EFP/EFR routes and no other.
states.bears_on: The operator's own rule enumerates where each shape may be executed. As of 2023 no clause admits open outcry for any of the five. Combined with the pit-era text (next two rows), this is the rule-level basis for `regular: &[]` on every one of the proposed keys in their current era.

states.verbatim: 524.A. "1. TAS transactions executed in the pit must be made open and competitively pursuant to the requirements of Rule 521 during the hours designated for pit trading in the particular contract and must be identified as such on the member's trading records. 2. TAS transactions on Globex may take place at any time the applicable contracts are available for trading on Globex." The eligibility list above the rule is split under two headings: "Pit-Traded Contracts" - "Light “Sweet” Crude Oil- spot (except on the last trading day), 2nd, 3rd and 7th months / New York Harbor No.2 Heating Oil ... / Natural Gas ... / NY Harbor Gasoline Blendstock (RBOB)..." (no Globex codes) - and "CME Globex Contracts", a table of "Commodity Code on CME Globex" values: WST, RTI, BHT, HPT, HHT, BBT, CLT, HOT, NGT, RBT, RET.
states.bears_on: CORRECTS the Pass-1 claim that no shape ever had an open-outcry route. NYMEX/COMEX TAS did, from 2009-09-14. But CME lists the pit route by the UNDERLYING's product name and the electronic route by the TAS root's own Globex commodity code, so the pit route is a pricing convention inside the underlying's pit, not a session of the `CLT`/`GCT`/`SIT` order book this crate would key. `regular: &[]` therefore still holds for the TAS keys - now as an adjudicated fact rather than an unexamined one.

states.artifact: NYMEX Rulebook Chapter 5, Rule 524 - archived editions bracketing the disappearance of the pit clause; and the same rule's TAM and MO sections
states.artifact_date: Editions observed at Wayback timestamps 2015-03-06, 2016-08-09 and 2018-02-05 (the timestamp dates the observation of the edition, not a rule change)
states.verbatim: 2015-03-06 edition, "524. TRADING AT SETTLEMENT (“TAS”), TRADING AT MARKER (“TAM”) AND MATCHED ORDER (“MO”) TRANSACTIONS": 524.A.1 still reads "TAS transactions executed in the pit must be made open and competitively pursuant to the requirements of Rule 521 during the hours designated for pit trading in the particular contract..."; 524.B (TAM) reads only "1. TAM orders may be entered on Globex at any time the applicable contracts are available for TAM trading on Globex and during each TAM contract's prescribed pre-open time period... 2. TAM-eligible commodities and contract months may be executed as block trades pursuant to the requirements of Rule 526."; and 524.C states "MO transactions are open outcry trades competitively executed pursuant to Rule 521 where the price of the trade is that day's settlement price for the contract." The 2016-08-09 and 2018-02-05 editions are titled "TRADING AT SETTLEMENT (“TAS”) AND TRADING AT MARKER (“TAM”)" and contain no occurrence of "executed in the pit must be made open".
states.bears_on: Three things at once. (a) TAM has never had a pit route, even in the pit era - so `regular: &[]` for every TAM key is affirmative, not inferred. (b) The TAS pit clause left NYMEX/COMEX Rule 524 inside the bracket 2015-03-06..2016-08-09; the bracket is stated, no day is invented. (c) The decisive contrast: in the SAME rule CME names its open-outcry shape as such - "MO transactions are open outcry trades" - and does not say that of TAS, TAM, BTIC, TACO or TMAC. The omission is contrastive, not silent.

states.verbatim: CME 2012-05-12 and 2015-03-19: "524. [RESERVED]" - and the string "Trading at Settlement" does not occur anywhere in the 2015-03-19 chapter. CBOT 2014-11-16: "524.-525. [RESERVED]". CME 2015-09-05: "524. Trading at Settlement (“TAS”) Transactions ... 1. TAS orders may be entered on Globex at any time the applicable contracts are available for TAS trading on Globex and during each TAS contract's prescribed pre-open time period." CBOT 2015-09-15: identical wording. CME 2016-11-22: "524. TRADING AT SETTLEMENT (“TAS”) AND BASIS TRADE AT INDEX CLOSE (“BTIC”) TRANSACTIONS", with 524.B.1 "Globex-eligible BTIC orders may be entered on Globex at any time the applicable contracts are available for BTIC trading on Globex and during each BTIC contract's prescribed pre-open time period." and 524.B.2 the Rule 526 block-trade route. Neither the CME nor the CBOT rule ever contains a pit clause.
states.bears_on: CME/CBOT-side TAS and BTIC never coexisted with a CME or CBOT futures pit: their governing rule was [RESERVED] until after the 2015-07-02 open-outcry futures closure, and it was Globex-only on the day it first appeared. That closes the pit-era question for grain TAS, livestock TAS, Treasury TAS, equity BTIC, TACO and TMAC without needing any argument from silence, and it dates each shape's Pre-Open language back to its rule's first edition.

TACO and TMAC are absent because they printed zero volume and zero open interest on 2026-09-04 (confirmed in the same day's ProductSlate) - an activity absence, NOT a CME classification statement, and it is recorded as such.

states.verbatim: TAS page: "To ensure appropriate and efficient messaging practices for TAS orders into CME Globex, the timing of each TAS groups' pre-open state is randomized. The market state sequence for TAS groups has a market pause, communicated via the market data Security Status message (tag 35-MsgType=f), tag 326-SecurityTradingStatus=2 at 16:00:00 on Sunday and 16:45:00 Monday through Thursday. TAS groups then go into pre-open on Sundays between 16:00:00 and 16:01:00 Central time (CT), and Mondays through Thursdays between 16:45:00 and 16:46:00 CT." TMAC page: the identical paragraph with TMAC substituted ("The market state sequence for TAC groups has a market pause ... TMAC groups then go into pre-open on Sundays between 16:00:00 and 16:01:00 Central time (CT), and Mondays through Thursdays between 16:45:00 and 16:46:00 CT.").
states.bears_on: CME states the Pre-Open in session-state language for the TAS and TMAC groups themselves, at the platform's Sunday 16:00 CT and Monday-Thursday 16:45 CT instants - the same queue onsets `cme_group.rs` already classifies as `order_entry`. The randomized 16:00:00-16:01:00 / 16:45:00-16:46:00 second is below this crate's resolution and is not encoded, exactly as the handoff decided for the energy TAS :30/:38 randomization. CAUTION recorded rather than smoothed over: the sentence is a blanket claim about "TAS groups", and grain TAS does not open until 19:00 CT on Sunday - so this sources the pre-open ONSET for the platform-default TAS groups and does not by itself fix the queue for a TAS family whose own open is later. Each family's Pre-Open still needs its own source.

states.verbatim: Under the heading "CME Globex Contracts": "For compliance and enforcement purposes, the start of a TAS pre-open period is defined by receipt of the security status message indicating that the group has transitioned to the pre-open state and the end of a TAS trading session is defined by receipt of the security status message indicating that group is closed. TAS orders may not be entered into CME Globex from the end of a TAS trading session until receipt of the security status message indicating that the group has transitioned to the pre-open state." The section's own product table lists "Pit-Traded Contracts" by underlying name ("Light Sweet Crude Oil (CL)", "COMEX Gold (GC)", "COMEX Silver (SI)", "European Gasoil (100mt) Bullet (7F)" ...) and "CME Globex Contracts" by TAS commodity code (CLT, BZT, BBT, ...).
states.bears_on: CME uses the words "a TAS trading session" - session language for the shape itself - and bounds it exactly as the crate does: pre-open state opens the order-entry window, the group-closed message ends the trading session. It also dates the pre-open/order-entry structure for NYMEX/COMEX TAS back to 2013, ten years before RA2302-5, and it is the document that most clearly separates the pit route (underlying code) from the Globex route (TAS code).

per_shape.pit_era_note: NYMEX & COMEX Rule 524.A.1, from its adoption on 2009-09-14 (MRAN RA0907-4) until a bracket of 2015-03-06..2016-08-09, read "TAS transactions executed in the pit must be made open and competitively pursuant to the requirements of Rule 521 during the hours designated for pit trading in the particular contract". This does NOT give the TAS key a regular session: the advisory's own tables list the pit route by the UNDERLYING's product code under "Pit-Traded Contracts" (CL, HO, NG, RB, BZ, 7F, GC, SI - no TAS code) and the electronic route by the TAS root's own Globex commodity code under "CME Globex Contracts" (CLT, BZT, BBT, HOT, RBT, NGT, ...). The pit route was a pricing convention inside the underlying's pit; the crate keys the Globex TAS instrument. It is also consistent with the crate's existing treatment - energy_metals.rs already ships regular: &[] for the NYMEX/COMEX outrights in every era, so no NYMEX pit is modelled as regular anywhere. WRITE THIS INTO THE MODULE COMMENT so the next reader does not 'discover' the pit clause and conclude the key is wrong.

conclusion: Author all thirteen-plus proposed trade-type keys with regular: &[] in every era, the published executable window in extended, and the shape's own Pre-Open in order_entry. Do not carry globex_equity_index's 08:30-15:15 CT CME_REGULAR onto any BTIC/TACO/TMAC key: CME excludes BTIC and TACO products from that family by name, and Rule 524 gives none of these shapes a floor route. Each module comment must name the channel its empty regular rests on (they differ per shape) and, for the energy and metals TAS keys, must record the 2009-2015 NYMEX/COMEX pit clause and why it does not create a regular session. U-4 is no longer a blocker for any shape.
dead_ends: CME's refdata API is inadmissible (401) - unchanged. The trading-hours service returns hasEvents:false for the TAS groups TG (gold), CT (crude) and CI (crypto) for the week 2026-09-06..2026-09-12, so it cannot source a TAS Pre-Open. There is no Client Systems Wiki text page for BTIC or TAM: a CQL title search returns only the attachment images "Basis Trade Index Close_BTIC" and "Trade at Marker_TAM", and title~"Basis Trade at Index Close" returns size 0 - so the pre-open-state paragraph that exists for TAS and TMAC does not exist for BTIC or TAM, and their Pre-Opens rest on Rule 524 plus the session service instead. ContractSpecs returns an all-"-" empty record for most trade-type productIds (8528 ESQ, 8407 GCD, 6266 CLL, 4346 GCT, 7891 ZCT, 10319 TBT, 10205 MCT): their hours live on the underlying's page. The r.jina.ai reader returns HTTP 429 under load; two saved files are that error body, labelled in INDEX.md. The ProductSlate `floorTraded` boolean is unusable - spuriously true across the contiguous id band 8914-8927.
follow_ups_for_issues: LAW-FOLLOW-UPS-ARE-ISSUES: the previous pass's INDEX.md for this gate asserts "There is no open-outcry route for any of the five shapes in the rule that creates them." That is falsified by NYMEX & COMEX Rule 524.A.1 (2009-09-14 .. 2015-03-06 at least). The Pass-2 addendum in the same INDEX.md corrects it; any handoff prose derived from Pass 1 must be corrected too.

U-0a (MCT): CME's ProductSlate names MCT - {"id":10205,"globex":"MCT","exch":"NYMEX","name":"Micro Crude Oil TAS"}. That is a CME statement of the product's identity and exchange, though not of its hours; it does not by itself close U-0a, which needs an hours statement.

BTIC row / U-1: EMT is listed as UNMAPPED and 'not sourced' in the handoff, but CME's slate carries {"id":7596,"globex":"EMT","exch":"CME","name":"E-mini S&P MidCap 400 BTIC Futures"} and the Daily Bulletin's BTIC PRODUCTS VOLUME REPORT prints an "ME" row (16 lots on 2026-09-04, 735 on 2026-08-20). Worth re-opening.

BTIC row / U-1: 6EB does not appear in CME's ProductSlate at all (6EP does). Either the FX BTIC root has been delisted or the slate omits it; the handoff maps 6EB to a new globex_fx_btic_euro key and this should be checked before the key is authored.

U-1 (EST envelope conflict): CME's trading-hours service returns closed@15:00 CT for EST's own group SB, which agrees with the "6:00 p.m. - 4:00 p.m. ET" BTIC line and not with the 16:00 CT outright envelope that ContractSpecs productId 7968 prints. A third CME channel now sits on the BTIC side of that conflict.

TAS Pre-Open per family: the wiki's blanket "TAS groups then go into pre-open on Sundays between 16:00:00 and 16:01:00 CT, and Mondays through Thursdays between 16:45:00 and 16:46:00 CT" cannot be the whole story for grain TAS, whose own Sunday open is 19:00 CT. Each TAS family's Pre-Open still needs a family-level source before its order_entry rules are encoded.

The exact day the TAS pit clause left NYMEX/COMEX Rule 524 is bracketed 2015-03-06..2016-08-09 and not stated by any document retrieved. It does not affect any encoded value (regular stays empty either way), so it is recorded rather than resolved.
